tier_reason: First-party README tables (Benchmarks section) compare Spinel-compiled binaries with CRuby 4.0.4 and CRuby 4.0.4 --yjit on the 28 listed scripts in benchmark/ (bm_*.rb), with gcc 13.3 and perf stat -r 5 stated, but the hardware is only a '32-core Linux box' with no CPU model and the repo has no timing script (make bench only checks output against CRuby), so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 13.3 builds the generated C; the README does not list flags, but Spinel's cc driver defaults to -O2 (src/main.c opt_level "2", Makefile COPT ?= -O2) plus -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -ffp-contract=off. CRuby 4.0.4 (revision b89eb1bc) run with --disable-gems, and with --yjit for the JIT column; each cell is the mean of five wall-clock runs under `perf stat -r 5`, measured 2026-09-17 on spinel 74c8e0a4.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers with only a core count for hardware; no timing script is checked in (make bench is a pass/fail output check against CRuby), so the perf stat runs are not reproducible from the repo as-is. Sub-10 ms cells are dominated by process startup (about 0.8 ms per binary; README says those ratios are lower bounds). The README itself warns the fib row (44.6x vs YJIT) reflects the C compiler folding a pure call tree at build time, not per-call speed. YJIT is essentially identical to the interpreter on mandelbrot, nqueens, matmul, partial_sums and sieve, so the largest multiples there are against an un-accelerated baseline. Spinel compiles a Ruby subset (whole-program type inference, no eval or dynamic metaprogramming), so the benchmarks are programs inside that subset. The geometric means (8.5x vs YJIT, 15.2x vs interpreter) reproduce from the 28 table rows (derived from page data).

notes: Record is accurate: every quoted cell (mandelbrot 18 vs 938 ms, matmul 6.1 vs 201 ms, binary_trees 2.7 vs 13 ms, json_parse 28 vs 133 ms, csv_process 95 vs 396 ms) matches the README, and recomputing the geometric mean over the 28 rows gives 8.51x vs YJIT and 15.21x vs the interpreter. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT (LICENSE, Copyright 2024- Yukihiro Matsumoto), 2.2k stars, 142 forks, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-10-06. Shortcomings: no CPU model, no checked-in timing harness, startup-dominated small cells, fib row constant-folded, Ruby subset only.
